title: A criterion for exactness through a fibre product

standard_prerequisites.name: Cartesian and cocartesian squares
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the projection from a fibre product is an epimorphism when the other structure map is one, which is how the epimorphism demanded by condition (2) is produced.

standard_prerequisites.name: Coimage, image and the canonical factorisation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definitions of the coimage and the image of a morphism in an abelian category
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the canonical projection onto the coimage, the canonical injection of the image into the kernel of the next map, and their compatibility.

core_obligations: Notation (proof lines 1163-1165): i is the canonical injection of the kernel of g, p the canonical projection of x onto the coimage of f, and j the canonical injection of the image of f into the kernel of g.

(1) implies (2) (proof lines 1167-1175): for h : w -> y with g h = 0, one factors h through the kernel of g and takes the fibre product of x and w over that kernel with projections k and l; the defining identity c k = j p l gives h k = f l, and since j p is an epimorphism the projection k is an epimorphism by the cited lemma, which is exactly condition (2).

(2) implies (1) (proof lines 1177-1182): applying the condition to the canonical injection i of the kernel of g provides an epimorphism k onto that kernel and a morphism l with f l = i k; comparing with the factorisation of f through its image and cancelling the monomorphism i shows that the composite of the injection of the image with the projection is an epimorphism, hence that injection is an epimorphism and therefore an isomorphism, which is exactness of the sequence.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the kernel, coimage and image maps attached to the pair of composable morphisms.
Build the fibre product to convert the exactness hypothesis into condition (2).
Apply condition (2) to the canonical injection and use the factorisation of f to recover exactness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a composable pair of morphisms in an abelian category to be exact, namely that every morphism into the middle object killed by the second morphism can be lifted through the first one after an epimorphism, with the lift and the epimorphism displayed explicitly (statement lines 1151-1160). The proof is a complete argument in both directions: the direct implication builds the fibre product of the two morphisms and uses that the composite of the injection of the image with the projection is an epimorphism (proof lines 1167-1175); the converse applies the hypothesis to the canonical injection of the kernel and cancels monomorphisms in the factorisation of the first morphism to conclude that the canonical map from the image to the kernel is an isomorphism (proof lines 1177-1182). The non-formal content is the construction of the fibre product and the final cancellation. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
